title: Then Came Sonny
seoTitle: Commanders 24, Giants 21: Sonny Styles' Stop, Stefon Diggs' Game-Winner and Jayden's First Two Picks
summary: Commanders 24, Giants 21: a slugfest, a second half that felt like the old days, Jayden's first two picks of the season, and then Sonny Styles and Stefon Diggs happened.
wireTaps: We won. On a Thursday. Brad Rogers and I broke the streak together.
paragraphs: First, to everybody at Högwaller last night: as much as I would have loved to join you, I knew my mind and body could not handle another late night with an early morning today. You were in my heart. I was in my bed. That's the trade you make at 45.
What a game. Commanders 24, Giants 21. Let me walk you through it the way I lived it, which was mostly horizontal.
## A Slugfest, As Advertised

This had all the makings of a low-scoring slugfest, and for a half it was exactly that. Both defenses were playing well. The Giants missed a 33-yard field goal. We got a field goal of our own, and then, with five seconds left in the half, Jayden found Ben Sinnott from a yard out. 10-7 at the break. By the end of the night the Ben Sinnott truthers on r/Commanders had come out of hiding, and honestly, they earned it.

Remember last week, when Jayden said you'd have to ask Blough why the tight ends besides Chig never catch the ball? A tight end besides Chig caught a touchdown. I don't know what was said in that building this week, but I think somebody asked.

A word on Cam Skattebo. I still don't think he's that good. At 45, I might average 4.0 yards a carry with the holes their line was opening up. He averaged 4.3. So I am three tenths of a yard from being Cam Skattebo. He did score twice, and every one of those holes is a reminder of how badly we miss Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne in the middle.
Going into the half, I felt good. Great, even.
## Oh, Here We Go Again

Then we came out of the locker room and I said, out loud, to nobody, "OHHHH here we go again." Our first drive of the second half went three plays and lost 15 yards: a 14-yard sack, a delay of game, and a punt from our own six. Jason asked the group chat what Dan Quinn said at halftime "to de-motivate the team this much," which is a fair question I'd like answered at Monday's press conference.

Here's where I'll correct my own memory, because my memory at 10 p.m. is not admissible evidence. I remembered a long Giants drive after that. It wasn't long. It was five plays and two minutes, ending with Skattebo going 13 yards untouched. Somehow that's worse. The long one was in the second quarter: 16 plays, nearly eight minutes, and a little piece of my soul.

To be fair to the guys, we answered right away. Antonio Williams took one 31 yards to the house, and a few minutes later Frankie Luvu punched the ball out of Malik Nabers' hands and Jeremy Reaves recovered at our 20. 17-14 us.

But it was starting to feel like the Redskins of old. We cannot cover a tight end. Isaiah Likely caught nine balls for 127 yards, and with eight minutes left, right after we turned it over on downs, J.J. McCarthy hit him for 66 yards and a touchdown. It was the longest touchdown of McCarthy's career, and the longest of Likely's career too. Of course it was. We have a real knack for this. Every week, somebody gets their "longest" or their "career best" against us. Somewhere there's a backup tight end circling us on the calendar right now. It's 21-17 Giants, and I'm doing the math on draft position in my head.
## Here Comes the First Pick

At 2:08 Thursday afternoon, I typed this into the group chat: "like I think JD even throws his first pick." Jayden had not thrown an interception all season. I'd like to apologize to Jayden, because I was right, and then I was right again.

On the next drive, we got all the way down to their 24 and he threw one into the end zone that got picked at the two. On the drive after that, he threw another one at midfield. I was still watching on my iPad, in the dark, when the second one happened, and I just set the iPad down on my chest and stared at the ceiling for a while. Jason typed "Seasons over," and then put it best: "It's crazy Jayden had zero picks all year and then does it on back to back possessions."

Both picks were thrown toward Chig Okonkwo. Chris had some thoughts about Chig that I can't put on a family website, followed by the fairest sentence anybody typed all night: "Maybe not his fault but still."
## Then Came Sonny
All the Giants had to do was run out the clock. They had the ball near midfield with about two minutes left and a four-point lead. A couple of handoffs, a punt, go home.
Then came Sonny.

Third down, right at the two-minute warning, McCarthy kept it around the left end, and Sonny Styles exploded J.J. McCarthy into tiny J.J. McCarthy pieces. Two-yard loss. Then the Giants punted, and the punt went 12 yards. Twelve. Out of bounds at our 29. That's not a punt. That's a handoff.
Sonny finished with 13 tackles. By the time I woke up, r/Commanders had a thread titled "Sonny Styles for President," and I'd like to formally endorse the candidate.

And it wasn't only Sonny. One drive earlier, the Giants tried to sneak Jameis Winston for a first down, Quinn threw the challenge flag, and they took it away. Then the Giants took a delay of game on the punt. And on that last Giants drive, Quinn burned two timeouts to stop the clock. This was a theme. At the end of the first half, Chris typed, "Dan Quinn accidentally had good clock management," and Jason thought Quinn was calling timeouts like he was "over compensating." Coach, after October, overcompensate all you want. I asked you to clock it. You clocked everything.
## Then Came Stefon

1:46 left, 71 yards to go. First play, Jayden throws deep for Treylon Burks and the Giants get flagged for pass interference, 33 yards. A scramble, a short one to Ekeler, and then Jayden hit Stefon Diggs over the middle for 32 yards and the touchdown with 57 seconds left. Three plays. 71 yards. 49 seconds. Jason's full analysis: "STEFONNNNNNN."

Chris made a point before the game that I keep coming back to: Jayden does his best when he has to. He's great all the time, but with his back against the wall he's downright surgical. Two picks, a ceiling stare, and then three plays for 71 yards. That's the guy.

Then, because we're us, Kain Medrano forced a fumble on the kickoff and the Giants recovered it anyway, and my heart stopped. McCarthy hit one for 21 yards to midfield. And then Rasul Douglas jumped a deep ball to Nabers at our 11 with 34 seconds left, and it was over. Three kneel-downs. We won. On a Thursday.
## Ref Watch: The Streak Is Over

Before the game I wrote, "Thursday again, Brad. Let's break the streak together." We did. Brad Rogers had us twice before, both Thursdays, both losses. Last night his crew threw four flags on us for 17 yards and six on the Giants for 62, ten total, under his 12.5 average. Brad was boring, which is all I ever ask.

We still found a way to give away yards before the snap: two false starts and a delay of game. Jason wondered if pre-snap penalties are a stat the NFL tracks, because he thinks we're "blowing by the NFL record." Jason, I have a whole page that counts flags. Next season I'm adding a jar.
## The Wave

If you want to know what it felt like to be a Commanders fan last night, read r/Commanders top to bottom. Before kickoff there was a post titled "Tonight's dilemma," which was the whole win-now-or-tank debate in two words. After the final whistle: "I still love Jayden!" "Apologize to JD5 by tomorrow." "Daronte Jones is the only one that deserves a job next season." "Did you abandon Ben Sinnott?" And my personal favorite, "Undefeated is undefeated," which, against the Giants, Jayden technically is.

The group chat was the same ride. That afternoon Jason said if we lost, "I'm 100% on the lose train." By 11:17 p.m. he had changed his tune: "I enjoyed the hell out of this I'm sorry." Chris, the man who wants us to bottom out and rebuild it right, replied, "Don't apologize for that. I did too." Nobody is tanking. Nobody was ever tanking. We just say that.

Jason's closing statement on the Giants: no issues with John Harbaugh, McCarthy "honestly was great tonight" even though he doesn't think much of him, and "Skateboo honestly I can't stand." Then, at 11:33, "When do we think Ben went to bed?" Jason, I was in bed the whole time. I was just also awake, holding an iPad over my face in the dark like a raccoon.
## My Number: 28-20

I picked 28-20, us. Final was 24-21, us. Right winner, four points high on us, one point low on them. I picked a winner again and the masochism paid off. Check the [leaderboard](leaderboard.html) and see where everybody landed, and if you called 24-21, please write in on [Roll Call](roll-call.html) so I can be appropriately jealous.
We're 3-5-1. The Giants are 5-3-1, which puts us two games back in the division with eight to play. Dallas is 4-5. Philly is 2-7. The NFC East still blows, and we're still breathing.
Now we get ten days off before the Bengals come to town on Monday Night Football. I'm going to spend them getting some sleep. Sonny is going to spend them running for president. Hail.
